source.title: Scaling Transformers for Discriminative Recommendation via Generative Pretraining
source.authors: Chun-Qi Wang; Bin Wu; Zheng Chen; Lei Shen; Bing Wang; Xiao-Yi Zeng

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests scaling in a new setting: discriminative recommendation, including a sweep of dense parameter counts and reported power-law fits. It does not reproduce language-model pretraining-loss or compute-optimal allocation measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports a discriminative recommendation scaling sweep, including AUC and loss values and fitted power laws, which bear on V5 and V6. Generative-model loss curves are not a scaling sweep. Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures loss and recommendation AUC across model sizes in a new training regime. Its CTR-XL sweep and fitted power laws test V5 and V6; its strategy comparisons also show conditions where downstream scaling weakens or reverses.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors: GPSD mitigates overfitting and improves recommendation scalability, with offset power-law fits on CTR-XL from 13K to 327M dense parameters. Their public-dataset discussion also acknowledges that the largest model is not always best, so consistent improvement should be confined to the reported industrial sweeps.
record.recipe_differences: This is a recommendation scaling study using generative pretraining, sparse transfer and freezing, followed by discriminative training. It measures recommendation AUC and task loss, rather than language-model held-out pretraining loss, and does not study token- or compute-optimal scaling.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported scaling behavior depends on training strategy: the paper says standard discriminative training has weak scaling, whereas FT&SF and ST&SF consistently improve across scales in most listed cases. CART gains at the smallest scale are marginal.

fits_no_version.finding: Same-size AUC improvements from transferring and freezing embeddings measure the benefit of GPSD, rather than predictability with scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generative pretraining with sparse-parameter freezing can improve discriminative recommendation at a fixed model size.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated scaling results. The power-law fit is reported for one large recommendation dataset and one described training strategy; no out-of-sample test of predictions from smaller runs is reported. The loss split/type is not specified with the Table 8 values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 3 FT and ST strategy AUC rows are omitted; the paper characterizes them as only slightly better than NT, and the selected Table 3 rows retain NT plus both sparse-freezing strategies to show scale behavior and the strategy contrast. Figure-only scaling results for HSTU and Wukong (Figure 6), public-dataset scaling results (Table 6), and architecture-comparison results (Table 4) are not extracted; the figures do not give tabulated point values and these results are not the fitted CTR-XL sweep.

untested.parts: No language-model held-out pretraining-loss scaling experiment.
No fit restricted to small runs followed by validation on runs orders of magnitude larger; Figure 5 fits the observed sweep.
No fixed-compute optimisation of parameter and token allocation or compute-optimal exponents.
No loss comparison across a wide range of architectures at fixed parameter count. Table 4 compares attention direction using recommendation AUC.
The fitted power laws cover one recommendation dataset and ST&SF regime; other modalities and power-law scaling in other training regimes are not established.
No quantitative relation between downstream AUC and pretraining loss, no language-task evaluation, and no held-out scale prediction.

Training strategies change AUC scaling, but the study does not compare fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits across setup or fitting choices, explain disagreement between published laws, or demonstrate residual departures from a fitted single power law.

record.verdict_notes: V5 evidence is an in-sample fit with an additive asymptote, without fit uncertainty or independent extrapolation validation. The dense-parameter axis excludes frozen sparse parameters, which grow from 125M to 4B; architecture and learning rate also vary. Table 3 rows collectively test scale trends, whereas their same-size NT baselines test transfer benefits. Public-dataset, cross-architecture and attention-direction results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they do not require missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: The scaling sweep is for discriminative recommendation, not held-out pretraining loss of language models; it does not test loss scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute with the other quantities non-bottlenecked.
Power laws are fit to the reported recommendation sweep, but the paper does not report using smaller runs to predict larger runs and then checking those predictions against larger runs.
No fixed-compute-budget allocation sweep or comparison of compute-optimal parameter and token counts is reported.
The paper varies model scale and some architecture dimensions together; it does not compare architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests a recommendation setting with generative pretraining followed by discriminative training; it does not test image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer in other domains.
Reports downstream recommendation AUC across scale, but does not test downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or on language-model downstream tasks.
Does not compare fitting methods, parameter-counting choices, training schedules, or data setups to test whether fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on them.

relationships.condition: CTR-XL recommendation with generative pretraining and ST&SF; 13K–327M dense parameters
relationships.reason: R02–R18 show decreasing loss and increasing AUC, with offset power-law fits reported in R17 and R18; the sweep jointly changes dense and sparse sizes.
relationships.display_finding: Loss decreases and AUC increases with offset power-law fits as dense and sparse model sizes change together.

relationships.reason: R01–R15 increase monotonically from 0.6306 to 0.7018 AUC, and R18 reports a fitted scale relationship.
relationships.display_finding: AUC increased monotonically from 0.6306 to 0.7018 across eight models and was described by a fitted scale relationship.

relationships.condition: CTR with FT&SF or ST&SF; CVR with FT&SF
relationships.reason: R23–R30 and R35–R38 show consistent AUC increases across all four sizes; these establish in-sample scaling trends without an extrapolation test.
relationships.display_finding: AUC increased consistently across all four sizes in each specified setting, without an extrapolation test.

relationships.condition: CVR with ST&SF, L4H32A4 through L4H128A4
relationships.reason: R39–R41 increase from 0.8110 to 0.8249 to 0.8326 AUC.
relationships.display_finding: AUC increased from 0.8110 to 0.8249 to 0.8326 across the three sizes.

relationships.condition: CVR with ST&SF, L4H128A4 to L4H256A4
relationships.reason: R41–R42 show a near-plateau, increasing only from 0.8326 to 0.8327 AUC; uncertainty is unreported.

relationships.condition: CART with FT&SF, all four sizes; ST&SF through L4H128A4
relationships.reason: R47–R50 rise from 0.7151 to 0.7437, and R51–R53 rise from 0.7146 to 0.7362; small same-size transfer gains at the starting scale do not weaken these scaling results.
relationships.display_finding: AUC increased from 0.7151 to 0.7437 with FT&SF and from 0.7146 to 0.7362 with ST&SF.

relationships.condition: CART with ST&SF, L4H128A4 to L4H256A4
relationships.reason: R53–R54 improve by only 0.0019 AUC, substantially less than earlier size increases.
relationships.display_finding: AUC improved by only 0.0019, substantially less than at earlier size increases.

relationships.condition: NT training on CTR and CVR, L4H32A4 through L4H128A4
relationships.reason: R19–R21 and R31–R33 show increasing AUC over the first three sizes, before the largest-size reversal.
relationships.display_finding: AUC increased across the first three sizes on both tasks before reversing at the largest size.

relationships.condition: NT training on CART, L4H32A4 through L4H128A4
relationships.reason: R43–R45 improve only from 0.7136 to 0.7168, showing substantially weaker scale gains than the freezing strategies.
relationships.display_finding: AUC rose only from 0.7136 to 0.7168, showing weaker scale gains than the freezing strategies.

relationships.condition: NT training, L4H128A4 to L4H256A4, on CTR, CVR and CART
relationships.reason: R21–R22, R33–R34 and R45–R46 show AUC decreases of 0.0035, 0.0031 and 0.0006 respectively; larger size fails to improve performance in these comparisons.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing width from L4H128A4 to L4H256A4 reduced AUC by 0.0035 on CTR, 0.0031 on CVR and 0.0006 on CART.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CTR-XL recommendation task, ST&SF, 13K–327M dense parameters
reader_labels.reason: The reported recommendation loss and AUC sweeps are fitted by power laws; see R01–R18. This supports the form in this new setting, not the original language-model pretraining-loss claim.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CTR-XL downstream AUC across the tested ST&SF model scales
reader_labels.reason: AUC rises across the reported dense-parameter sweep and the paper fits a power law to that trend; see R01, R03, R05, R07, R09, R11, R13, R15 and R18.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: CTR and CVR with FT&SF or ST&SF, L4H32A4 through L4H256A4
reader_labels.reason: The reported AUC values rise with scale for both freezing strategies on these tasks; see R23–R42.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CART with FT&SF or ST&SF, especially at the smallest scale
reader_labels.reason: At L4H32A4 the results are only slightly above the NT reference, while larger scales improve; see R47 and R51.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: No-transfer (NT) training on CTR, CVR and CART
reader_labels.reason: The largest model's AUC is below the L4H128A4 value on all three tasks, so increasing scale is not consistently beneficial without the proposed transfer-and-freeze strategy; see R22, R34 and R46.
